reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical derivation rests on embedding human joint kinematics into the projective space P3. By representing joint axes as lines via Plücker coordinates, we construct a 6x6 motion matrix M. For a two-joint system (waist and shoulder), the motion space MS is constrained to a 5-dimensional hyperplane (p12 = -p13). The central duality lies in the relationship between geometric alignment and linear algebra rank. When the waist-shoulder line L aligns with specific planes or axes defined by the shoulder joints, the rank of the system drops. This rank deficiency is captured by the support set supp(p), which enumerates the axes with non-zero coefficients in the unique 1-dimensional dependency relation among the joint axes. The failure mode, or 'redundancy collapse', occurs when supp(p) shrinks from its generic size of 5 (excluding the uncompensatable sideways bending X) to smaller subsets like {Si,Y,Z}. In the empirical context of cricket bowling, this collapse manifests as a direction cosine approaching zero near ball release. The injured bowler exhibits this prolonged collapse (~30 ms), whereas the uninjured bowler maintains full support. Thus, the primitive operators translate a continuous biomechanical trajectory into a discrete sequence of algebraic ranks, providing a rigorous, geometry-based metric for overuse injury risk that bypasses traditional force-moment calculations.
